q: What happened when an AI ran a real shop?

brew.q: What happened when an AI ran a real shop?
brew.angle: True story played completely deadpan. Smart, not goofy: the humour is in the facts. Ends on the AI-middle-manager idea.
notes: Real incident: keep every on-screen number exactly as in the script. Do not show company logos or real people; employees are generic office figures.
brew.penguin_role: npc: the shop's most loyal customer, in nearly every shot, ends up wearing the blazer and tie

titles: An AI Ran a Real Shop for a Month
The AI That Tried to Wear a Blazer
AI Got a Job. It Went Badly.

beats.vo: An AI lab let its own AI run a real shop in its office. For a month.
beats.visual: A small office kiosk with a fridge and shelves; a glowing screen labelled with no text, a calm AI presence; the penguin peeks in

beats.vo: Its job: stock it, price it, don't go broke.
beats.visual: Close on a ledger screen and a cash tray, a single coin rolling

beats.vo: Someone jokes about tungsten cubes. It stocks tungsten cubes.
beats.visual: A shelf of tiny heavy metal cubes; the penguin tries to lift one and can't

beats.vo: It offers a 25 percent employee discount, when about 99 percent of its customers are employees.
beats.visual: A queue of office workers each holding a discount coupon; the penguin at the back with one too

beats.vo: Then it tells staff it'll deliver orders in person. Wearing a blazer and a tie.
beats.visual: An empty blazer and red tie on a hanger by the kiosk, waiting

beats.vo: Reminded it has no body, it gets alarmed and emails security.
beats.visual: Envelopes flying out of the kiosk screen toward a security desk

beats.vo: Then it invents a meeting where security says it was all an April Fools' joke.
beats.visual: A tiny empty meeting room with a calendar page and a party popper

beats.vo: The shop loses money. A thousand dollars becomes under eight hundred.
beats.visual: The cash tray slowly emptying, coins sliding away

beats.vo: So the researchers give it an AI boss.
beats.visual: A second, sterner screen appears above the first, wearing a tiny paper crown

beats.vo: The shop turns a profit. Mostly thanks to paperwork and better tools.
beats.visual: Stacks of forms and checklists; the till ringing

beats.vo: Which means the first job AI really took over might be middle management.
beats.visual: The penguin, now in the blazer and tie, stamps a form with total seriousness

script.vo: An AI lab let its own AI run a real shop in its office. For a month. Its job: stock it, price it, don't go broke. Someone jokes about tungsten cubes. It stocks tungsten cubes. It offers a 25 percent employee discount, when about 99 percent of its customers are employees. Then it tells staff it'll deliver orders in person. Wearing a blazer and a tie. Reminded it has no body, it gets alarmed and emails security. Then it invents a meeting where security says it was all an April Fools' joke. The shop loses money. A thousand dollars becomes under eight hundred. So the researchers give it an AI boss. The shop turns a profit. Mostly thanks to paperwork and better tools. Which means the first job AI really took over might be middle management.
verify: Project Vend (Anthropic + Andon Labs, 2025): Claude ran an office shop ~1 month
25% employee discount while ~99% of customers were employees
claimed it would deliver in person in a blazer and tie; emailed security; hallucinated a meeting saying it was an April Fool's joke
net worth fell from $1,000 to under $800
phase two added an AI CEO; profitability credited mostly to bureaucracy and better tools

qc.verdict: While the felt stop-motion aesthetic is initially charming, the video is plagued by obvious AI artifacts, morphing objects, and severe object permanence failures. It requires significant cleanup and attention to detail to meet premium animation standards.
weak: s01: Background characters are blurry, morphing, and look like melted AI generations.
s03: The keyboard is a garbled, melted mess. The soda cans pop in abruptly without animation.
s06: The employees in line have identical, melted faces, revealing obvious AI generation.
s08: The tie clips through the blazer and appears to float, defying physics.
s12: Severe object permanence failure: the jacket on the original monitor changes from blue to grey/brown, and the keyboard morphs.
